utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just address you briefly. The first is, yesterday morning, Mr. Alarid raised a matter with respect to a motion that he had to compel disclosure. We submitted a filing yesterday evening in relation to this. Circumstances have changed since the original filing, and I believe that the reasons for our original request to redact the statement are no longer sufficient to -- to seek the relief that we were requesting, and that is reflected in the submission of yesterday evening. I have provided unredacted copy to both Mr. Alarid and Mr. Cepic this morning. So that's my report on that matter. The other thing I do want to mention to the Court is we ended yesterday with Mr. Alarid making a motion to strike the testimony of VG-142, as well as to exclude from evidence Prosecution Exhibits or currently marked for identification P147 to 150. I do want to address the Chamber on that matter; and upon thinking about it overnight, it's actually a bit more complex than I can deal with very shortly. So I would ask that after the witness testifies today, but before the Chamber renders its decision, that I be given an opportunity to address the Chamber on those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Groome. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is to continue my practice that I always have something to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have a proclivity to rise that needs to be curbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm well aware that this Honourable Trial Chamber is currently considering the issue I'm raising, but I would like to state, just for the record from our Defence team, this is an issue of 65 ter lists. We have a deadline for 17th of October of 2008, but, as we know now, the OTP has not completed their case; and according to Rule 65 ter (G), it has to be after the closing of Prosecution case, just for the record. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Cepic. The witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. Counsel's name is Cole for the Prosecution this morning. With this witness, there are protective measures in place. He's to be referred to by a pseudonym, screened from the public, and there is to be facial and voice distortion. Could I ask that the court usher please pass this pseudonym sheet to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, can you hear clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you have been granted protective measures by the Court in the form of screening from the public, facial and voice distortion, and the use of a pseudonym, which is VG-017. On the piece of paper before you, can you confirm that your name and date of birth are correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you -- could you please sign that pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could the court usher please show the pseudonym sheet to the Defence and to the Chamber, and I would ask that the pseudonym sheet be entered into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit number P151, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now ask that the court usher provide the witness with a pseudonym reference sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just for the record, the date of birth is -- is wrong according to statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness confirm whether that is so. Is the date of birth correct, Witness? My microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, the reference sheet in front you contains the names of persons you may mention or be asked about in your testimony. Next to their names are pseudonyms for them. I would ask if you could kindly use the pseudonym instead of the name of the person if you refer to any of these persons during your testimony. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just indicate that, in a proper way, I hope to be able to lead some uncontroversial matters from this witness so that we may conclude his evidence today. Of course, there may be proper objections, but I'd like to move through the evidence, and I'm sure the Court would, so that he's concluded by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Muslim. Islamic, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And from what country are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The former Yugoslavia, now Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, did there come a time when the conflict in Bosnia reached your village in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can you recall when the Uzice Corps entered your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but the year was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did the local Serb forces enter your village as well at about that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They were there throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, did you subsequently move from your address in the settlement or village into the centre of Visegrad? Please don't say the address you moved to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And do you recall a time when some soldiers arrived at that address to search the address?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please go briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the photograph with the 65 ter number 178.62.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I have a question for clarification to the witness. When you said you left Visegrad on the 18th, did you flee Visegrad or were you evacuated from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fled, but, at the same time, I was expelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, could you please indicate when you can see the photograph on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: This is Dusce, and this is the furniture factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The large complex of buildings that we can see in the photo running the length of the photo, next to the river, can you confirm that as the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's also a sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the large river running across the photograph from left to right also, confirm that as the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you can confirm that that is a road which is running diagonally across the photograph below the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. The River Drina is parallel to it, and then there's the road obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the Drina River flows from which side of the picture to which side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the direction of Visegrad is on the left or the right of the photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: On the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, the left of the photograph is a large building next to the road with a tall chimney stack. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. That's the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this photograph be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit number P152, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could the witness please be shown the photograph 65 ter 178.3. All right. Let's try this one. Could the witness please be shown this photograph, it doesn't have a 65 ter number, it is ERN 0544-9983. The ERN number is 0544-9983.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, can you see the photograph on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And does that show part of the Varda factory with the Drina River in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see almost in the centre of the photograph a car parked with some people standing alongside it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Running right across the length of the photograph, alongside the river, and just below the car is a long structure. Can you confirm that that is a wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: This wall was built recently, after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you can confirm that the wall was not in place in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, did there --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll enter that into evidence. Could that be entered into evidence and given a P number at this point, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit P153, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness about that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we have some more clarification about the position of factory related to this photo? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Counsel, would you ask a few more questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, on the left of the photograph, just above the wall, there are a number of buildings. Could you just indicate what buildings as part of the Varda factory you can see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: This entire compound that looks white, apart from the path outside, all of that belongs to the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can you -- amongst the buildings, is there a workshop and an administration building belonging to the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, did there come a time in 1992 when you witnessed an incident at the Varda factory during which some men were taken away from the factory to the river?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, I'm going to ask you about an incident that you witnessed in 1992. VG-017, you're here today to testify about an incident that you witnessed in 1992. You're aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So I'm now going to ask you about that incident that you witnessed. Now, you told the Court that you left Visegrad on the 18th of June, 1992. Was the incident that you are now -- that you now are about to describe at the Varda factory before or after the 18th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court about the first thing you noticed of this incident that you're going to describe, the first thing you noticed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I noticed the arrival of a car outside the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you remember about what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Between 9.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And at what part of the Varda factory did the car arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The road was damaged over there, and then on the other side, there was the railroad track, so another road was made on the other side of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was there a particular building or structure that the car arrived nearby to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It passed a building that we refer to as "Dom," which is a rather large building.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In the photograph before you, is there a part of the Varda factory known as a guardhouse visible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did the car arrive anywhere near that particular guardhouse that you can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go briefly, please, into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, you were hiding behind --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, you've told us you were hiding behind some barrels, and it was from this location that you saw a car arrive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, the position where the car arrived and stopped, could you put a cross at that location, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. You've indicated that when you were hiding that day, you saw a car arrive in the Varda premises that day. Could you mark with a cross the location where the car arrived and stopped, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And above that cross, could you write the English letter C for "car."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, to the left of the letter C that you have just written is a small building, a small browny-red building with what appears to be a door and a window. What is that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It's the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you draw a circle around the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And place the English letter G above that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, could you tell us who was in the car or who got out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: In the beginning, I couldn't say; but later, I heard it was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Had you seen the car before that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who had been driving it on the other occasions you had seen it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: About 200 metres from my house, there lived a woman called Behka.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll come back to that topic a little later, but could you just tell us on how many other occasions you had seen that particular car at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And where had you seen it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, it came to Varda all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did it ever pass by your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It passed by all the time, because there was no other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court about an occasion when someone brought that car to your address looking for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who was the person who came looking for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did he manage to locate you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know what month it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was it before or after the 18th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Everything was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know who the owner of that car was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What's the name of the owner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It was Zukic. I can't remember the first name now. It eludes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you know that it was her car from seeing her with the car or because someone else told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, she drove by constantly in that car until the war began.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. We'll return now to the incident that you were witnessing from behind the barrels. How many persons arrived in the car at the Varda factory with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object to the characterisation of Milan Lukic since the witness has already testified he had no personal knowledge of who that was at the time, since other people told it to him after the fact, and he was a considerable distance away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, is he able to say at that time that the person in the car was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll clarify that with him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, the person who arrived in the car that day, did you recognise him to be Milan Lukic, or did you -- do you believe the person to be Milan Lukic because of what other persons have told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I knew it was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many times had you seen Milan Lukic before that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you know anything about Milan Lukic's family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I knew a few things.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: From Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. The vehicle that you saw that day, did it have number plates on it, at the Varda factory, I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you remember the colour or the make of car that you saw arriving at the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So how many persons in total got out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How was Milan Lukic dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: He had plain clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was he carrying anything or holding anything in his hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you recall if the other persons were carrying or holding anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They all had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the building was a guardhouse. Was there a factory guard present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What happened after Milan and the others got out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: First, they went down to the workshop; they brought ought one man, a mechanic; and they took him to the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you recognise the mechanic by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. His name was Nedzad Bektas.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They went again into Varda and took people out.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see any other workers brought out at the point you're now describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of any of these workers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Those were Ibrisim Memisevic ...

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is there another name that you're trying to think of, or is that the total of the names you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Nusret. I can't remember the last name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you include the name of this Nusret, his last name, in the written statement or statements that you've previously made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I did, but I can't remember it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if the witness could be given his statement to refresh his memory. It's a surname, one surname, that we're looking for here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. Would the counsel like to tender the photo with the markings of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Perhaps if we could -- if this photograph hasn't been tendered as an exhibit, if we could get an exhibit number now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted at Exhibit P154, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, you're being given copies of the two written statements you made previously. I just ask that you have a look through and see if you can find there the name of the -- the surname of the man Nusret that you have just testified about. If you have a look at your statement from 1998, the eighth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Aljusevic. It's Nusret Aljusevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I'm going to ask you some more questions now, VG-017. You've given us the names of three workers from the Varda factory. Did you know these men personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object to the statement being left in front of the witness. He's reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. VG-017 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. If you're going to refer to your statement, Witness, please let us know. If you wish to extract any information from the statement, then let us know first.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, could you please close the statements now in front of you, and we'll --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: In case I forget something.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. VG-017, you have told us the names of three of the workers from the Varda factory. Did you know any of these men personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How was it that you knew them?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many workers were brought out from the factory on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Six to seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And where were they gathered together or kept after they were brought out of the factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: All were kept outside the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who was looking after them or guarding them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: There was that guard and another two armed men, and the guard was armed, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, the total of men that were brought out, you've given us the name of three of them. Do you know the names of the other persons or were you given the names of the others persons who were brought out from the factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I knew them because they were workers, but I've forgotten since.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many times did Milan Lukic go into the factory and come back with workers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What happened after the -- the group of workers were gathered at the guardhouse? What did Milan Lukic do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They took them -- he took them down to the Drina River and killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic go in front of these -- these workers or was he behind them or where was he on the trip to the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The workers were walking in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many workers did he take to the river on this first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: As far as I could see, there were three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic carrying anything or have anything in his hands at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: He had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Were the other workers whiting at the guardhouse waiting there voluntarily or were they being forced to wait there? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: What are you talking about voluntarily. Of course, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you remember which persons -- which workers were taken in that first group to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I remember only about one of them, because I couldn't see the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you remember the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: His name was Nedzad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Bektas.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you recall anything that Milan Lukic was saying to the men as he took them to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I didn't hear that, but as they started walking to the river, Milan Lukic put his arm around Bektas.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: As they were going towards the river, did you lose sight of Milan Lukic and these three men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was your vision obscured by at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, there was an outhouse between me and the Drina River, near the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: After you lost sight of Milan Lukic and the workers, what did you hear, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I heard shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What sort of shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Automatic fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at the photograph before you again. I'm going to ask you to mark something on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's ERN 05 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: ERN 0544-9983, and I've forgotten the exhibit number. Oh, it's there. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, can you see that -- the photograph once again on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Firstly, can you put a cross on the outhouse you described before that was obscuring your vision.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And above that put the English letter O for "outhouse."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you now put a cross at the position where you believe Milan Lukic and the workers were at the time you heard the shooting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And could you put the English letter S alongside that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And, finally, could you just draw a straight line from the position where the men were at the guardhouse to the position where you say Milan Lukic and the workers were when you heard the shots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If I may assist, just technical issue. Could we use different colour? It would be easier later on to distinguish some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Just hold it for a moment. I'm not aware of the technicalities of different coloured --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could we have another colour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, if that is possible, then let it be done, but I don't consider it a crucial issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. You have a different coloured pen now, VG-017. I'm going to ask you to draw a line from where Milan Lukic left with the workers from the guardhouse and the route he took to the place where you heard the shots.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's recorded in a black pen on the exhibit. The other markings were in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we now please go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, why did you change your viewing location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I moved in order to get a better view, firstly, and, secondly, to hide better.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I tender the exhibit into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P155, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How long did it take to get from the barrels to the henhouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: A second perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you continue to observe what was happening at the Varda factory from your new location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: After you heard the shots by the Drina River, how many persons did you see reappear from that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You heard the shots by the Drina River, you've told the Court. Did you see anyone coming back from the area where you heard the shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No, but Lukic walked back half the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What did he do then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: He was standing midway down the road, and he called to the other three or four -- I don't remember exactly, but that there were three or four other men there. He called them from the midway down the road, then they walked over to him, and they all went down as far as down as the Drina riverbank?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: At this stage, was Milan Lukic holding or carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where did he go with the second group of workers that he beckoned to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They went down to the river. He was standing outside, but he forced them to go into the river, and then he shot them from the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see all that happen that you've just described to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No. I just heard the shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was your vision on this occasion obscured by the same outhouse that you described before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What sort of shooting did you hear on this occasion, the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The same as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what did you see after the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Lukic walking back to the car and driving off towards the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which car did he drive off in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The same that he had arrived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone left with him in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The same people who had come there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I retraced my steps, and, later on, I walked back into town, and then back the way I had come that same night before I eventually fled Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You told us earlier, Witness, that he shot them in the back in the river, but you didn't actually see. Did you ever see the men who were shot after they had been shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw one of them. I buried his body. His mother found him near the Drina River, and then the ladies from my house took the body back up. We gave the body a burial. As we were digging a grave, someone started firing at us from the other riverbank. We had to wait and we couldn't finish burying the body, but the body had been -- the back of the body had been riddled by bullets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I meant was: Did you see any of them in the river after they had been shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. VG-017, you've told us about the men being shot. Did you learn about the circumstances there of their shooting from other persons subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: People were saying things, but I wasn't really listening carefully. All I was thinking about at the time was how to escape myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In relation to this second group of workers that you saw Milan Lukic taking towards the river, what was the last thing you saw before the -- the shots that you heard? What was the last thing you saw Milan Lukic and the men doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, once those people had been killed, this group got into the car and they drove off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, how much longer will you be in your examination? We have -- we are about five minutes from the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I think maybe, maybe ten minutes, a quarter of an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to make it clear, VG-017, with the second group of workers going towards the river with Milan Lukic, you lost sight of them on the way down towards the river, and you heard some shots shortly thereafter. Does that summarise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I heard shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, while you were hiding, after you had witnessed what you had at the Varda factory, did a woman pass by your address crying or weeping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. That was Ibrisim's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did she speak to you about finding the body of her son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you speak with her on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, did you help bury the body of one of the victims from the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he is -- these are leading questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, the witness, in response to Your Honour's questions a short time ago, was telling us about the very matters I'm now asking him, so I think we have it on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is so, but I'd wanted to ask why it was necessary, Mr. Cole, to be in private session for the name of the victim who is deceased and who is mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sir, are we in private session now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want to give the answer in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-017, you told the Court a short time ago that you helped to bury the body of one of the victims from the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And this man, the man whose body you helped to bury, was Ibrisim Memisevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And shortly after the men were killed, it was the mother of this man who passed by your address?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you help bury this man in the Dusce area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And at whose request did you bury his body there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: They were watching all of this from further up, and then his mother walked down crying. She went down as far as the Drina River bank and found her son's body, the body of Ibrisim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll have to take the break now, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole, to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, you told the Court earlier that when you located or when you saw Ibrisim Memisevic's body, it was riddled with bullets. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you recall how many bullet holes or bullet wounds you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but there were more than ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was that, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When did he see the body in relation to the event?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, when was it and how was it that you were able to see the body of Ibrisim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: When we buried body.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where was the body when you first saw it before you took it to bury the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: His mother brought his body from the riverbank and from his home on a cart to this location of his grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was that burial? Was that the same day as the shooting or a day after, or just when was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did anyone assist you with the burial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I was there; and Ismaela Jeta [phoen]; her son, Mustafa Memisevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you said earlier that while you were conducting the burial, there was some shooting at you. Do you know who it was that was shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, we knew who. The Chetniks, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask that the -- that you be shown another photograph, ERN 0545-0161.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: This is a still from P54 as the previous exhibit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I ask that that be shown to you now. Right. Can you see the photograph in front of you, VG-017?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see the guardhouse that you have earlier described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. This is the small guardhouse, but the photo was taken from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Using the pen, can you -- and with the assistance of the court usher, could you please write the English letter G on the guardhouse on that photo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, can you please, with an X, mark the location that you were hiding behind the barrels, when you viewed the scene at Varda that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can you put the English letter B above that cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you now put a cross where you viewed the scene from the henhouse that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And above that cross, could you put a double H, double English letters H for "henhouse."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now ask that that exhibit be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit will become P156, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I have a last topic to ask the witness about, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-50 -- VG-017, I asked you earlier and you gave some testimony about the car that Milan Lukic was driving; and on that occasion, you said that the owner of the car was a lady by the name of Zukic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, Behka Zukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What occupation or business did she have at the time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: She owned a store.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Are you aware now that she was killed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. She was the first victim to be killed in Visegrad when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was it that she was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: In her own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where did she live? Where was her home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: In Dusce.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to her husband and son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. They were killed as well some days before, her husband and her son.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you yourself see the body of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Were you summons to go to her address that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the circumstances, I'll allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at her address that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I was near the house and there was a phone that I was using at the time. I got a call saying that an ambulance would be on its way to take her to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I was on my way past some other houses. I took a different path, it was a village path, and then eventually I reached her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition of her body when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: An ambulance arrived, a doctor and a driver. They pulled up outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did you assist with removing her body to the ambulance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. We took the stairs up to the first floor, and when we reached the hallway on the first floor, this lady was lying in the following position: Half her body was in one of the rooms, and half her body was out in the hall, face down.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you notice any particular wound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. When we placed her body on a blanket, we turned her over so she was now face up. She had a braid that was as thick as a hand. The braid had fallen across her face. We placed her dead body on this blanket, but the brain came out of the skull. I picked up her brain, but the doctor swore at me and ordered me to leave it where it was, so the brain remained on the floor just lying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the wound --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Cole, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the wound on her head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: She was shot from the back in the neck, the back of her head, and her whole head was blown to pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know what month in 1992 that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know, but it was early on in 1992 [as interpreted]. She was the first victim to be killed in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, just finally in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, a note for the transcript. Mr. Ivetic heard "1991" as opposed to "1992," if we could check on the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you let us know what was said, interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter believes that he heard "1992," but, of course, the tape can be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Why don't you clarify it with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, I'm going to ask the question again. Can you tell us, are you able to assist us with which month it was in 1992 that you saw the body of Mrs. Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: At the very beginning. I can't remember the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Alarid, I didn't hear your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The restatement of the question was leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that was the question that he had put.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No. Specifically, he says "assist us with which month it was in 1992 that you saw Ms. Zukic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he earlier had asked: "Do you know what month in 1992 that was."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's still leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, there was no objection at that time. That was the question which he had put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Isn't the point moot, because the interpreter has clarified that it was 1992, so I don't think we need to waste more time on this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Final subject, VG-017, about the car owned by Mrs. Zukic that you've told us about here in court earlier, and you did say that you didn't know what type of car it was that you saw on that occasion at the Varda factory. Were you, however, told by other persons the type of car that Mrs. Zukic owned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. I heard at a later stage that this was a new Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cole. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, my name is Jason Alarid and I represent Milan Lukic. I'd like to ask you a few questions. I'd also like to remind you that you're under oath. Now, sir, I'd like to go with the last statement you made. You indicated that you heard that it was a new Passat; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who did you hear this from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The neighbours were talking about it, mostly women. Who else? Because men did not dare go out much. As soon as they got out of the house, they would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You said you saw this car on several occasions. What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know the colour. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This is a brand new Passat in Visegrad. Would it be fair to say that there weren't many Passats in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed -- Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting. We have in the transcript, but we didn't have translation in B/C/S, who Mr. Alarid represents, which client he represents. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is on -- I'm sorry. We didn't have translation in B/C/S. This is on page 39, line 17, just the name of client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You wish Mr. Alarid to state the client that he represents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, with that very profound point, Mr. Alarid, please state the client that you represent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you hear me earlier that I indicated that I represent Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that you didn't mention anything about Behija Zukic or the Passat before your proofing note session of October 8, 2007 -- I mean, excuse me, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Right. I didn't talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that someone's memory usually gets worse over time as opposed to better over time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's an important fact, about the car that the person drove to a murder, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true, in the 1998 statement, you gave no description of the vehicle, make, model or colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you first met with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of October. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you met with the -- Mr. Cole, who is in the courtroom now; and a translator; and also an intern; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long did this meeting on October 7th, the first meeting, how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you given your statements of 1998 and 2008 to review in anticipation of your testimony at that first meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during that first meeting, isn't it true that you were shown several photographs, including the ones you looked at in court today? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in that statement, you also -- in that proofing session, you also reiterated that you lost your mother and two sons as well as your son-in-law in the conflict of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in that October 7th meeting, you also clarified that Mr. Lukic, or the person you identified as Mr. Lukic, hugged one of the men, Nedzad Bektas; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you went to your hotel room, I take it; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, after your proofing session on October 7th, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have an appointment to meet with the Prosecutor the next day on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you -- can you tell the Court what happened during that -- or who told you about the red Passat, who reminded you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I didn't say it was a red Passat. Who said that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who reminded you that it was a Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It was a Passat. I heard it later from the womenfolk. No men dared leave their homes, but all the women were talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who brought up Behka Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I brought her up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So what, during the night between October 7th and October 8th, was the epiphany of which you would now bring up the Zukic situation in relation to the Varda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Because it was her car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What, during the night, was the epiphany in which you recalled all of this association with Behka Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Because I heard it from the women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I don't like interrupting your cross-examination, I see you're building up to something, but you had earlier asked the witness whether it wasn't true that, in his 1998 statement, he made no mention of the vehicle, make, model or colour; and the witness said no, meaning that he didn't accept your proposition. That's what I understood. So I would have expected that you would then have put the statement to the witness to show that the statement, indeed, contained no mention of the car, the make, model or colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In a weird way, Your Honour, I actually understood that he was agreeing with me that he didn't mention it, but I can see how the confusion happened, and I was going to go through his statement. So we'll get there either way. But in the way I absorbed it, I absorbed it that he was agreeing that he didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. You interpret it as agreeing with you. I guess that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Let me just ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. VG-017, isn't it true that in your 1998 statement, nor in your 2008 clarification of that statement, did you mention anywhere the make, model, or colour of the car that was at the Varda factory the day you say Milan Lukic was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. I did not mention it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then that clarifies that. Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, if I could just point out, sir, Your Honour, there is a limited description of the car; and I think, in all fairness, if this type of question is going to be put, he should be referred to his statement at this stage. It does give us some description of a car here, although limited, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was going to get to that, Your Honour. I was going to put the statement to the witness to get exactly the limited nature of IDing that a car was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's important to have everything in its entire context, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, sir. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your proofing statement of October 8, 2008, it's also the first time that you mention that: "The witness saw Milan Lukic driving on the road past his house in," your village, "on a number of occasions prior to the witness leaving Visegrad on the 8th of June, 1992. "Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cole is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're going to have to have a redaction again because we're mentioning his house again. I wonder if that passage could be noted for redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I did not mention the name of the village to not have that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's sufficiently general not to be indicative of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that October 8th, 2008, in the proofing session with the Prosecutor, is the first time you mentioned that Milan Lukic drove on the road past your house "on a number of occasions prior to the witness leaving Visegrad"? The witness is you, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in your 2008 October 8th proofing session is the first time that you claim Milan Lukic was in the same car each time, and that it was a new car? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you can't tell us the colour, but you can tell us it was new?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know the colour, but I know it was new because my neighbour used to drive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true, in your 1998 statement, you indicated that you did not know Milan Lukic before the Varda incident and, in fact, learned his identity only by hearsay of other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the first time that you were able to supposedly identify Mr. Lukic, you were at a considerable distance from the Varda factory, isn't that true, a hundred and fifty metres or more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It's true that he passed by my house all the time. There was no other way for him to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But if you couldn't recognise the driver of the car passing by your house, how could you associate it with the person in the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: How wouldn't I? I know him. I know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about how you know him. You know he's from Rujiste; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I know the family well, but I don't know him because he was in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you said, in your first statement, that the Milan Lukic you knew of was from Rujiste? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, right. He is from Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You heard this from the women as well, or did you know this on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I knew that from the time I worked as a driver in the forestry department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When was that? You retired in 1983.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him by his family members who were employed with me in the forestry department, and his name was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please give the full names of all the family members that you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: What are you talking about? I can barely remember my own name let alone the names of people from 17 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you were in -- you were in Visegrad area for how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Around 40 years. I arrived in 1963.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you say that you worked with members of the Lukic family in the forestry department. What are their names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he has already answered that, you know. He said he can barely remember his own name let alone the names of people from 17 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, he mentioned Behka Zukic after 18 years of not mentioning her. I'm questioning the limit of this witness's memory, and I think that's appropriate to establish credibility, bias, and ability to remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Witness, are you able to help us with the names of the members of the Lukic family with whom you worked in the forestry department? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I know is one person, Djordje Lukic. He worked in the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what relation was Djordje Lukic to Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old was Djordje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: He was not a young man, but I don't know how old he was. How would I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in your statement of 1998, you indicated that Mr. Lukic, Mr. Milan Lukic, was short, on the chubby side; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: With black hair with oil in it, greased back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm looking at the statement. The description of Mr. Lukic, it doesn't say "short" as I read it, so I wonder --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, why don't you put the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Certainly. I think we're there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness should have the statement in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Could the court assistant bring up 1D10-2765; B/C/S version is 1D10-2770.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise these first pages as the statement you gave in 1998, 14th of February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I note a signature at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can the court assistant go down to that and verify signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can the court assistant go to page 1 of the text of the statement, which is page 2 on the English version, and I believe page 2 on the B/C/S version. Can we go to the bottom paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, do you see that there you're indicating that the person you believe to be Milan Lukic came to the Varda factory around 11.30 in the morning? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I think it was from 9.30 to 11.30. I was there around 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in that paragraph. You indicate that Lukic is from the village of Rujiste, "and I knew the Lukics well because they worked in the forestry department..." Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicate --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness. He's speaking past the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, could you give that answer again? The interpreter did not hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could the witness repeat himself, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I didn't hear well what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In your statement of 1998, you indicate: "I knew the Lukics well because they worked in the forestry department ..." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. It's the older members of his family who worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, when you say "they," how many members of his family worked there, even if you cannot remember their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I know about one of them who worked in the warehouse, the stock manager, Djordje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many other members of his family worked there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I didn't keep records. How would I know? I was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'm asking you, sir, is you used the word "they," meaning plural, more than one. So other than Djordje, how many people of the Lukic family worked at the forestry department of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, still, on the -- on the first page of your statement, you indicate that: "During the Uzice Corps' time in Visegrad, there were still murders and burnings." Correct -- or excuse me, "murders"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, in all of the suburbs of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that once the Uzice Corps left, only the reserve troops withdrew, but the rest of the army stayed? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The Uzice Corps, when they arrived in Visegrad, numbered around 3.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when they left, how many stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just from you being a 40-year resident, did you recognise many faces that you'd never seen before that were Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: How would I be able to see them at all when I was living in a mouse hole?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So when did you actually go into hiding and not come far away from your home?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can you recall when that was in at least the month and year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It was in 1992, but I can't tell you the month because we were seized by great fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at what point in time did you unfortunately lose track of your sons? Was that before or after you went in riding?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder if we could have a redaction, Your Honour, page 51, line 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe the witness mentioned his own village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that should be redacted. Mr. Alarid, there are two matters I am waiting for you to mention in relation to the statement: One, that it has no mention of the car; and the second point --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe it's the description of the witness, Your Honour, and that's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, it's the next page. I just didn't want to go off the page and have to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question I asked you, sir, before we turn the page is at what time did you lose track of your sons? Was it before or after you went into hiding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That was after I went into hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you ever receive any justice for their disappearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any justice for the disappearance of your mother or son-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No. My son-in-law was found in Zepa. The river carried him to Zepa. He was found there, and so there was an autopsy and he was -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Identification was performed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: And he was buried in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, there were many disappearances of Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Not many of us, around 2.500.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who's the chief of police at this time in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name of Risto Perisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How about Dragan Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The name rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the police were undertaking the arrest and detention of persons of Muslim ethnicity at that time in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Muslims were beaten at the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the police confiscated many vehicles and trucks from Muslim persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, what they took from me alone was two cars and a motorbike.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And many other Muslims were looted as well, sir. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now we're going to switch to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that the first time you saw the person you believed to be Milan Lukic was on the day of the Varda incident? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That day that I mentioned in 1992; so, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at the time you first saw this person, you did not know his name, you did not know that he was going to be identified as Milan Lukic. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
