utterances.text: And even on the day that you say he had come by your home, you didn't see that person, did you, nor did you see the vehicle that this person came in; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I saw everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: From where you were hiding in your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I was on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And where would you be able to see, especially since you do not describe it in your statement of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: How on earth could I have not seen it? I was sitting on a chair in the room on the first floor, and the window was wide open. You need to climb about five or six stairs to reach my house in the first place, but I noticed the car down there and saw Milan Lukic walk up the steps. I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the last part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer, sir. The interpreter did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: When I heard the car pull up outside the house, I saw Milan Lukic get out of the car. I was sitting on a chair, and the window was open. I went out the window since the window was open, and the window was on the side of the house, and then I hid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the reason I -- I believe that you did not see it is because if you read the paragraph describing this incident, you state, "Apparently, he was asking for me by name." And "apparently" indicates that you didn't hear it, but you were told that by someone else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Who else could have said that? He was the only person in the house. Everyone else had fled. I was hiding by night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, then, if no one's there, how is he going to ask for you by name? There's no one to talk to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you indicate that this Lukic is about 30 to 35 years old. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I did say that, but I didn't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "He is of medium height and on the chubby side." Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you go on to say that he had darkish hair with oil on his hair. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you go on down to say that: "I saw that Lukic was wearing civilian clothes when he came on that day." Are you indicating the day at the Varda factory or the day at your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: At my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So, on the day of the Varda factory incident, what were the people wearing that came to the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Some JNA uniforms, olive drab, and some -- the other kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The reason I'm confused, sir, is if you go down to the second paragraph, it indicates that basically one person and three other men call, and then you said that, "I don't know the three soldiers that he was with. These three wore the camouflage uniform and some had the SMB uniform." "Some" indicates more than one person to me, so it appears that there were more than four by that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I only saw three.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the person that you believe to be Milan Lukic at the time, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Civilian uniform, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please describe the civilian uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you remember colour of pants or colour of shirt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No. How on earth could I possibly remember that sort of thing? I was doing my best to get out of the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he wearing a jacket or a hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Perhaps. Perhaps he was wearing a jacket, but I think his head was bare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We're getting details now that shouldn't be part of a public session. If could I ask, on this page, there be some redactions, I think from the question on page 56, line 12. We start talking about working and socialising at that point, and if counsel could be careful, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid. You do have to be more careful. So we have to redact those sections. The court deputy will note that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do we have to go into private session to mention any of the deceased or persons that this witness believes were taken out, because we are in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, I'll be advised by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. You Honour, the names of the victims, I don't believe there's any need for those to be in private session, if that's what counsel's asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what about Cancar Musan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I knew him by sight, he was or familiar face, but not his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you, from your vantage point at that house or the henhouse, could you tell Cancar? Could you identify him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you're positive that you saw Nedzad Bektas; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Of course. He was the first to be taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you also mentioned Ibrisim. Could you tell him from a distance, or did you learn that later from his mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you indicated that you helped bury Ibrisim; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Right. The moment they brought him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The moment the women brought him to the burial sight, is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you couldn't tell Ibrisim at a distance from where you were in the henhouse or your house; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question and the answer are a little ambiguous, in my submission, similar to a question and answer before. I wonder if any event if the counsel could be a little bit clearer in his question as to the occasion to which he refers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, how about, could you read the last paragraph of page 3 of the B/C/S statement, please -- or actually second to the last, sir, which begins with "Lukic." In middle of the paragraph, it appears to me that you only learned of the identity of Ibrisim later from his mother, not that you identified him directly at a distance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I see you're asking me about plenty of detail here. When they took him as far as the guardhouse, he knelt down, and his family over there, the wife and the children, were across the fence. He was looking at his children, and they called him and then he walked over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't this true that this is the first time you mentioned that about Ibrisim in any statements, including in the proofing sessions, and earlier in testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No. But you're making me say it, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, sir. I don't believe I'm putting those words in your mouth. You just indicated that that's what you believe. Isn't it true that you did not witness the incident at the Varda factory but heard the entire thing from other people and want simply to help those people find justice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I was positive, and my evidence is 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we please put on witness statement of 15 April 2008, uploaded as 1D10-2775. But before we do that, I would like to tender the 1998 statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the statement you've just gone through?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, then, you should put it to him that nowhere in the statement is there any mention of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I can do that, Your Honour. We'd need to back up. Are we already on the next?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, just, sir, isn't it true that nowhere in your 1998 statement do you mention a make, model, or type of car, correct, the statement we've just gone through, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, what we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you should further question him now as to how he came for the first time to mention the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I thought I'd asked him that in terms of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It follows more logically now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, in the written statement, he does refer to some details about a car. Now, counsel is asking him questions about the car without the witness being able to look at the detail that he has included in his statement. Now, in fairness, and the statement is now going to be admitted, certainly the English translation gives these details: "It was a ..." --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's on page 3 of the English version, sir, the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could that be shown -- shown for us to see?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's page 3, directly under the paragraph describing Lukic as 30 to 35 and chubby side. So we have to go back to the earlier exhibit. That would be 1D10-2765.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, is this at paragraph 12?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sir, in fact, we're talking about the earlier statement. It doesn't have paragraph numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was going to go on to the 2008 -- I was going to go on to the 2008 where he further clarifies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear now about the 1998 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there anything in it about the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That was a proposition that you had put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph two, Your Honour, of that page 3. He came to the Varda factory with three other men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just a moment. Your Honour, as part of my objection, I'd like to point out two features here, and counsel is compounding matters by putting unclear or ambiguous propositions to the witness. Now, in this paragraph, as we can see here, he has given a limited description: "It was a new car, the newest type of limousine." Now, that's a description of a car. That's quite something other than no description of a car at all. And second matter that I would like to raise an objection about is counsel's proposition to the witness that he had said Milan Lukic was short.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just a moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I corrected myself in reading out the statement that it was medium.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now these are points, of course, which you may raise in re-examination, Mr. Cole, quite properly. It doesn't mean that you can't raise them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, continuously during these sections in which you have participated, I don't know why you do so, but I would recommend you that you really faithfully cite the passages to the witnesses, because you have contributed continuously to confusion by altering the text that you are cited and, on many occasions, combining texts that are additionally confusing the situation. So I will expect you from your professional integrity, when you refer to transcript put to the witness, please do carefully your work before. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, part of the reason why you get into that difficulty is that when you're using previous statements, you must put the statements in front of the witness. Have the statements put in front of the witness. Judge David's points are well taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I take the admonition. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you read the second paragraph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you gave a description of a newer kind of limousine. What do you mean by "limousine"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: A new car. What else could I say? Limousine, white, a new car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Don't you think, from your vantage point of the house, it would be easier to tell colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true, though, if you had known this car to be Ms. Zukic's car and also seen it driven past your home on several occasions, that should have been something that was fresh in your mind in 1998, as opposed to being disseminated to the Prosecution just a couple days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The car drove past, and we all knew who drove it, and we all knew who the car belonged to, and that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder if we could have the witness's age redacted, page 62, line 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't the question I asked you. What I asked you is, if you had seen this car personally, also knowing it to be the car of Ms. Zukic, before the incident at Varda --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- if you had seen it and known it, shouldn't this have been something you disseminated to the investigators in 1998 as an important fact for this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't mention it at the beginning, and then the next time I did. I know this for sure, that this car belonged to Behka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could now the witness be shown 1D10-2775 -- well, actually, Your Honour, could we tender the first exhibit, the first statement 1998, into evidence at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D10-2765 will become Exhibit number D163.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, sir, as we go to that, isn't it true that in your first statement, you didn't know if this incident had happened in April or May? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, in fact, in your first statement, you indicated that it was at the beginning -- or excuse me, end of April, beginning of May, best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: At the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But in your --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go down to the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, just a correction. The previous Exhibit is 1D63.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall giving a statement April 15th, 2008, to the ICTY, as a clarification of your 1998 statement ten years earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in that -- in that meeting in April, you were asked if you could fix the date more accurately. Who were you asked this by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant show the witness paragraph 9, page 2 of that statement, and they are numbered paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I ask you to read the last sentence of that, and ask you if it's correct that you do believe it was between May and the sixth month. What does that mean? Clarify please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So are you stating that it could have been any time during May or any time during June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's all I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could release go to paragraph 12 on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in that statement, you indicated that you cannot recall the colour or make of the car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, again, wouldn't this have been an excellent opportunity to mention Ms. Zukic or that it was her car or that you had participated in the burial or removal of her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I participated in the removal of her body, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, but, sir, what I'm asking you is, when you were in this proofing -- or this statement session in April of 2008, isn't that an excellent time discussing -- even if you couldn't know the make or model of the car, discussing that you knew whose car it was and, in fact, had seen that car on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. This car belongs to the lady named Zukic. I saw it at least twice or three times, and Zukic's first name was Behka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that Ms. Zukic's car was important to proving this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then, again, wouldn't it have been an excellent opportunity in April of 2008 to have brought up Ms. Zukic's vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Well, how should I know? No one asked. That's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you please read paragraph 13 for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: You want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: "I saw Milan Lukic for the first time only after the war began. When he came to Varda factory and killed seven people, I didn't know his identity. I learned only later from other people that it was Milan Lukic."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who told you it was Milan Lukic? Who were these other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: The first was Smaila, the mother of Ibrisim who was killed, but I knew him myself by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I thought you hadn't really seen him before this moment at Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I saw him coming into the Varda factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was the first time you saw this person who you described in your statement as being 30 to 35, and on the chubby side, of medium height; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: That is true, but I knew him from seeing him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When and where did you see him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I saw him when the war began, when he started going around Dusce, when the killings started.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, you said you know -- you knew a lot of people who worked at the Varda factory. Did you know a Sevko Ustamujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. He was the chief of the locksmith workshop, or the supervisor, whichever you want to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant please put on the screen 1D10-3184, and what I really want the witness to look at is the last page of the B/C/S statement, which is a map written by Mr. Ustamujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Other than going through Mr. Ustamujic's statement, some of the names which he mentions in his name, Mr. Ustamujic is a purported eyewitness to the Varda shooting. On June 10th, 1992, he drew a map, identified Mr. Nedzad as one of the victims, and Cancar. In collaboration with this witness, or at least in sync with this witness, however, he identifies two other assailants perfectly and does not identify Milan Lukic. So going through the statement, maybe 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You would then be in excess of the time that I had in mind. The Prosecutor spent an hour and 35 minutes, and you would have the same time as the Prosecutor. After the break, you will then have about 25 minutes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, sir, this was a map that was attached to a statement by Mr. Ustamujic, and it describes several buildings of which I believe were in the picture that you started circling on. What I would ask you is, first, to look at this map and see if it accurately reflects the area, although I note the guard shack is not written on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I can't find my way around this map. I can't remember any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we bring up the photograph, please, that the witness marked up. I believe it was P153, and I believe the marked one is P154, which might be a little bit better reference for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, I put to you that you have a D over the -- or excuse me, a G over the guard shack, that little building out in the middle of the yard; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that that building in the foreground closest to the river, next to the left of the guard shack, is the mechanical shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, and the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that white building just to the left of that, isn't it true that that's the upright saw or the JGR building, plant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It's the administration of the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And further off to the left and off the screen is the saw hall and then the main Varda factory; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we bring the map back on the screen, please. I'm again referring to 1D10-3188.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, so, now that you've had an opportunity to look at the picture, even though this map is not to scale, is it relatively accurate as to the position of the mechanical building as well as what you call the administration building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: As far as I can see, that is so. It's so, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where would you put the guard shack?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If the court assistant could assist with the pen, the witness, I'd ask him where he would place the guard shack.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the road. That's the river. Maybe somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that the guard shack that you put in the -- in the photograph that you circled, is that where the guard shack would be in relation to the mechanical building and the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I can't see where the guardhouse is. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm conceding that the guard shack is not on this map as you circled it on the photograph. I'm asking you to draw the guard shack where it should be in relation to the mechanical building and the administrative building, as well as noting the workers' entrance and car entrance which are noted on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't do any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If the witness cannot, I can't push him any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That takes care of my objection, the witness's answer. Thank you, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we're going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, since I am moving on, I would like to tender the witness statement of 15 April 2008, which is 1D10-2775, B/C/S 1D10-2780, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure. I think, Your Honour, that's the statement of Mr. Ustamujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The statement of Mr. Ustamujic is a Gorazde sector SUP statement from the 3rd of April, 1996 that was tendered with the packet of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can I just be clear, then, which statement counsel is seeking to be admitted now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The supplemental statement by this witness of 15 of April 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as 1D64, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, sir, before I move on further, I would like to refer you to a statement made by you earlier in your testimony, when I queried you about basically: "Then, again, wouldn't it have been an excellent opportunity in April of 2008 ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go to the transcript page 66, lines 1 through 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: "Then, again, wouldn't it have been an excellent opportunity in April of 2008 to have brought up Ms. Zukic's vehicle?" Your answer was: "Well, how should I would know? No one asked. That's all I can tell you." So what I'm asking you, sir, is: Who asked you this week about the Zukic vehicle that might have refreshed your recollection to mention her in your most recent proofing session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I wanted myself to mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we bring up 1D10-3184, the statement of Mr. Ustamujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, sir, while we're bringing that on the screen, how well did you know Mr. Sevko Ustamujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know him to have been working through June of -- of 1992 at the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Assuming he had been working inside the factory, would you defer to his recollection of the death of Cancar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ask another question. It doesn't help whether he would defer to the recollection of somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Ustamujic had given a statement regarding the shooting of Cancar Musan and Nedzad Bektas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had you heard of an earlier kidnapping from the Varda factory that occurred approximately 15 or 16 days, on May 25th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's a redaction matter, if I could, on page 71, line 9. It's giving an indication of his association with the Varda factory. I wonder if we could have lines 9 to 11 redacted -- well, in fact, lines 7 to 11, because there certainly the English is a little bit ambiguous; 7 to 11 on page 71.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The reference to the Varda factory, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's an indication that it may indicate his connection with the Varda factory. There are all sorts of matters that are coming out now, but by putting them together, it can paint a picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, yes. The court deputy will present that for the redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The date of the shooting that you witnessed at the Varda factory, you indicated that it may have started -- or the incident might have started any time between 9.00 and 11.00. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you see a freight vehicle with a yellow tarpaulin arrive at the front gate of the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that the area that we're -- or that you've described today is not the front gate of the Varda factory? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know how to describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the area where the guard shack is known as the workers' entrance and not the front entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No. It's only the entrance to the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that that's where the workers at the sawmill would enter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Not that gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know Muho --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I haven't heard the name well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's Podzic, P-o-d-z-i-c?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Podzic, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. He was the manager at the sawmill in Varda.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you know Ramiz Karaman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes. He was the foreman in the timber section.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, did you know some Serbians named Nenad Tanaskovic, otherwise known as Neso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Vaguely. I seem to remember he was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, actually, wasn't it Slavko Trifkovic that was one of the Varda drivers before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I can't seem to recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know some workers at the factory named --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if, just in case I do mispronounce, we could go to page 2 of the statement in B/C/S and English, as the names are written on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'm looking at the middle of the page, sir, of at some names of the workers at the factory. Do you know a Nusret Dzafic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know an Islam Cero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a Husein Mujakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you did know Nedzad Bektas; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the aforementioned workers witnessed Nedzad being taken away by Tanaskovic and Trifkovic, what would you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Mr. Ustamujic did not mention Milan Lukic being present on June 10, 1992 in the abduction and killing of Nedzad, what would you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: You should first ask him where he was hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If he was in the factory, would that be a better vantage point than where you were in hiding by the barrels and the henhouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, "in the factory" could be anywhere, and, with respect, it's not an appropriate line of questioning. "If I were to tell you," we don't know what the basis of that is; but, I suppose, in summary, Your Honour, it's just not an appropriate line of questioning to put some hypothetical issue to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. I agree, Mr. Alarid. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And going to page 3 of the statement for the names, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a worker, Abdulah Hamak [sic]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: It's not Hamak, it's Jamak. Yes, he was a warestock worker in the workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you know Memis Cancar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's collection: Warehouse not warestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know Camil Kesmer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This person that you claimed to be Milan Lukic, did you ever get a look at his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did he have any facial hair or distinguishing features that you could notice from that vantage other than what you've already described in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: He was clean-shaven.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would tender 1D10-3184 into evidence, and we would have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I presume the counsel is talking about the statement of Mr. Ustamujic which we can see on the screen. In my submission, just because counsel runs through a list of names and puts them to a witness, and here even getting a no, in most cases is not a basis for admission of the statement of a person who is not a witness in this case into the evidence through this witness. There is no relevance that I can see. On top of that, I think some notification that this statement will be part of the Defence cross-examination came through at about 9.00 this morning. So if there's any suggestion it might be admitted, I would certainly like the opportunity to read it. If I could just have a moment. So, first, just summarising, it hasn't been shown that it's relevant in any way, and, of course, counsel is free to call this person as a witness if he wants to get this evidence before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. On those two points, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think what's important is that - and, you know, I know the Prosecution has made this caveat before - is that they're sort of not responsible for the content of statements that they've, in fact, tendered to us through the discovery and disclosure process. However, what we do have is a signed and regular statement of the witness that I think, on its face, is -- is very reliable. I think certain points within the statement, with regards to this witness and his knowledge of the persons at the Varda factory, have been confirmed, and, of course, some have been denied; and I wouldn't have expected otherwise from someone who had been retired interest the factory for 10 years prior to the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But the point being made is about the statement that you're seeking to tender now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would simply tender it as a statement that is inconsistent with the testimony of the witness, that is otherwise regular on its face, and within a fact that we are operating in a Tribunal that doings accept hearsay, and foundational issues that I think would make admission of this proper. In the alternative, Your Honour, I would ask simply that the map be attached, the handwritten map, as an alternative, but I believe that it is proper for the entire statement to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is an age-old issue in the Tribunal. Let us see how we will decide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I believe we marked the map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, anything more on this point, particularly if you have anything from the jurisprudence of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I don't have any jurisprudence, but if I could make these points, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Firstly, statements --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Firstly, sir, I don't have anything from the jurisprudence point of view; but, of course, statements and material is disclosed to the Defence with good and bad. We don't select what goes outs, so not everything supports the Prosecution's case, of course. Now, the statement in question, the witness hasn't read it, I presume. He hasn't been asked. Counsel hasn't read it. I don't know if the Chamber has read the contents of it. In any event, the witness didn't agree that he knew most of the names that were contained in the statement that was put to him. It hasn't been authenticated. Presumably, it's the statement of this man, but it hasn't been authenticated. There is the process of 92 bis or 92 ter or calling, potentially calling, the witness viva voce, if counsel wants to do that. In relation to the map that was drawn, as I recall, the witness did make a mark on the map; but, then, with counsel's concession, which was that he concedes the guard shack was not on the map, so the focal point of this is not even on the map. Then I think the witness, and I haven't looked at the spot, but I think we would find the witness wasn't able to help in the end. He was summarising a little bit confusing, the map. So, in total, my friend, with respect, hasn't substantiated why this witness statement should be introduced into evidence through this witness. There's -- the connection is far too tenuous and I would object strongly. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Briefly, Your Honour. Simply, I think we've offered this staple not necessarily for the truth of the matter asserted because that's for a later date, and I can see that to raise the level of reliability of this statement for the Chamber's purposes; and, of course, you're in the position to gauge the weight or credibility of any piece of evidence that we submit. However, we did put this to this witness, and I think from an impeachment of -- of this witness, it is proper; and without the other safeguard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he denied everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, but what he -- but what he did was he did admit that some of these workers were there. And what I find surprising is we've been presented with a witness that has no reference to the actual date and time as noted in the indictment. Here, I've submitted a witness statement taken before this witness ever gave his first statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have no authentication of this statement, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I mean, again, it appears regular on its face, and I think it could be you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down. The French booth really cannot follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we are not with you on this one. The points made by the Prosecutor are valid, in our view; and something that occurs to me, personally, is the total lack of authentication. You may, of course, call this person as an a witness in your case, should you be called upon to present a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and I agree, Your Honour. I mean, in all due diligence, we do have to follow up on these leads when they come up. I mean, I think that's very important, and that's why I was hoping at least to tender it at this point, not for the weight, understanding the limitations --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly asked to slow down when speaking. The interpreters cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... your cross-examination. Any re-examination Mr. Cole -- sorry. Mr. Cepic, you wish to --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just very few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very few questions. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. My name is Djuro Cepic, and I appear here for Sredoje Lukic as his Defence counsel. Before I proceed to question, I wish to say on behalf of Sredoje Lukic and all our Defence team that we sympathise greatly with all your loss and suffering, the loss of your sons in particular, and other members of your family. Let me go back to just one part of your evidence. You said you had known Djordje Lukic, and I have just a few more questions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Your Honour, it's a redaction matter here, and it may be preferable, if we're going to go into intimate details about relationships with people at particular small locations. That it be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Be careful, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you bring that for redaction. It's to the hotel, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Perhaps, if we could have it in redaction from line 19 down to where I lodged the objection. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll try to do my best to avoid any problem in that relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let us just go back to my question. Along with you and that gentleman with whom you played bingo, there was also a policeman from Visegrad, Sredoje Lukic, also playing bingo at the same table; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Of course, you know that Djordje Lukic had sons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you knew his son, the policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That was police officer Sredoje Lukic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, he was a very good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry. Almost the totality of the witness's evidence has been about a particular factory, so I think we're going to have that redacted as well. So that's page 81, line 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just to inform my learned friend, Mr. Cole, Visegrad had 11 factories before the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we will redact it ex abundante cautulae.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then, sir, you will agree with me that, during the war, you had not seen this police officer Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-017, in cross-examination by counsel for Milan Lukic, it was suggested that you couldn't, from your vantage spot at either behind the barrels or in the henhouse, see Ibrisim Memisevic at the Varda factory being taken out by Milan Lukic. You understand what I'm saying there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see Ibrisim Memisevic being taken out of the factory by Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, that concludes your evidence. We're grateful to you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And are we in public session? Yes. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just a brief point, Your Honour, because I did want to clarify for the Court why I even tendered this statement to the witness, of one the other persons. It's simply because on the memorandum to the Court that the Prosecution tendered to all of us indicating the witnesses that were going to be called this week and the documents that were going to be used through them, or potentially used through them, the witness statement of Mr. Ustamujic was identified as being used through this witness. So it was on that pre-set that I pursued the line of questioning and actually requested the tendering of the statement because -- and somehow they indicated the relevance by putting it in the list of documents to be used through the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. I want to deal with some procedural matters. First, you'll recollect that during the testimony of VG-142 yesterday, I indicated that the statements that had been challenged by Mr. Alarid would be marked for identification pending the cross-examination. No evidence was adduced in the cross-examination that would bar their admission, and those statements will therefore be admitted. Now, I move next to some other matters relating to the case as a whole, and I want to give some dates. The close of the Prosecution case and the disclosure required by both Defence teams to the Prosecution are expected to take place on the following dates: The close of the Prosecution case is anticipated to be Thursday, 6th November; the 98 bis submissions will be presented on Tuesday, 11th November; the Chamber's judgement on those submissions will be rendered on Wednesday, 12th November. Pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), from Thursday, 13th November, both Defence teams will permit the Prosecution to inspect and copy various items in the custody or control of the Defence which are intended for use by the Defence teams as evidence at trial. Pursuant to Rule 67(A)(ii), on the 13th of November, both Defence teams will provide to the Prosecution witness statements of all witnesses the Defence teams intend to call at trial, and copies of all statements taken pursuant to Rules 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater. In view of the above, the Chamber varies its previous order regarding the filing of Rule 65 ter (G) submissions by the Defence. Both Defence teams will now file their submissions pursuant to this Rule on the 13th of November. In the event that the Defence of both accused are called upon to present their case, on Thursday, 20th November, Sredoje Lukic will present his case, will commence the presentation of his case. The Chamber recalls that on the 15th of September, it made an oral ruling in which it decided that, as a result of granting Milan Lukic's request for a four-day sitting week and scheduling a two-week break between the 13th and the 22nd of October, there would be no break between the Prosecution and the Defence cases. Milan Lukic has requested reconsideration or certification to appeal this oral ruling on the basis that counsel needs more time in order to adequately prepare his defence. The Chamber considers that the Scheduling Order just presented sufficiently addresses any need for more time to prepare Milan Lukic's defence. In particular, it notes that Milan Lukic will not be required to present his defence until after Sredoje Lukic. The Chamber also considers that no clear error of reasoning has been demonstrated, and, moreover, that it is not necessary to reconsider the earlier decision to prevent an injustice. Furthermore, the grounds for granting certification for appeal as set out in Rule 73 are not met. This Chamber, therefore, denies the request for reconsideration or certification to appeal. Those are the matters I wanted to deal with, and you may now call the next witness if there is one. No?
